    CHAPTER I

The measurements were first published in that year,[1] and the
results were at once disputed by several of his rivals abroad.

A second series was undertaken the following summer,[2] though
the weather was against the observers from beginning to end.

Footnote 1: The second lecture of the Institute, delivered in May.

Footnote 2: The charitable bequests made in that year alone came
to a considerable sum, as the appendix shows in some detail.

    CHAPTER II

The numbering begins again in the second chapter of the book,[1]
as was the common practice among printers of that period here.

A second note appears in this chapter as well,[2] and the series
closes there without any further additions being made to it.

Footnote 1: Communicated at a meeting held in the School of Arts.

Footnote 2: The lecture delivered before the University at Oxford
in the month of June, and printed here for the first time now.
